http://www.jpost.com/international/artic.text: Moldova's foreign ministry condemned the violation of the country's airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Monday, it said in a statement on social media.Moldova shares a border with Ukraine and supports that country in Russia's war in Ukraine. It has dealt with numerous incidents of drones flying over its territory and debris near the border.The aerial object entered Moldovan airspace at 1737 local time (1437 GMT) and exploded shortly after, near the settlement of Talmaza, close to the border with Ukraine, Moldovan authorities said. The explosion set grass on fire but there were no casualties, they said. They did not identify the origin of the object."This incident constitutes a serious violation of the sovereignty of the Republic of Moldova and poses a direct risk to the safety of our citizens. Such incidents are unacceptable," the foreign ministry said in its statement.In separate incident, Russian drone shot down over Romania An F-18 fighter on a NATO air policing mission shot down a drone that illegally breached Romanian national airspace, the fourth unmanned aircraft shot down over the country this year, Romania's Defense Ministry said on Sunday.A spokesperson for NATO's military headquarters, US Army Colonel Martin O'Donnell, said the alliance is constantly on watch and prepared to defend itself from any threat. "Additional details regarding Sunday’s incident remain under investigation, but the drone appears to be Russian," he said.

https://www.witn.com/2026/08/20/warsaw-p.text: Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WARSAW, N.C. (WITN) - Warsaw police have arrested four men and seized five guns they believe are related to a series of shootings in Duplin County. Police stopped a vehicle Monday night and found the five guns inside. Those were two Glock handguns, two Draco-style firearms, and one AR-style rifle. Chief Darius Bentley says the Glocks were both equipped with automatic switches. Je’avion Newkirk, Dyan Owens, Kamari Sloan, and Nolan Smith are facing multiple firearm charges, including felony possession of weapons of mass destruction. Earlier this summer, authorities said there had been at least a dozen shootings in both Duplin and Sampson counties. In June, the ATF offered a $5,000 reward for information in the case. Newkirk, Owens, Sloan, and Smith are being held without bond, police say. Copyright 2026 WITN. All rights reserved. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/11/a-ma.text: Menü Kereső A Magyar Falu Programból pont oda jutott a legtöbb pénz, ahol a program egykori kormánybiztosa indult a választáson Belföld Sajó Dávid Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Az előző kormány a Magyar Falu Programot vidékfejlesztési programként állította be, valójában azonban főként önkormányzati felújításokra költött, a támogatások elosztása pedig politikai szempontokat is követett, állítja a Lőrincz Viktória országgyűlési képviselő, illetve vidék- és településfejlesztési miniszter. A politikus szerint ezt egy, még az előző kormány megrendelésére készült tanulmány is alátámasztja. A kormányzati értékelés szerint a programnak nem volt megfelelően meghatározott, számonkérhető célrendszere. A tanulmány egyik megállapítása szerint „nem férhető hozzá nyilvánosan olyan tervdokumentum, amely tartalmazná az elérendő célokat, és monitorozható lenne az eredményesség”. Lőrincz szerint emiatt a Magyar Falu Program inkább egy önkormányzati beruházásokat finanszírozó támogatási rendszer volt, mint hosszú távú vidékfejlesztési program. Lőrincz szerint a források elosztásánál politikai szempontok is érvényesültek, és különösen sok pénz jutott Gyopáros Alpár választókerületébe, ahogy az a politikus által posztolt térképen is látszódik. A politikus a posztja alatti kommentben még azt is kiemeli, hogy az ország „legszegényebb, és legelmaradottabb” térsége Győr-Moson-Sopron megye harmadik választókerülete, utalva arra, hogy ez a térség közismerten a jómódúbbak közé tartozik itthon. Gyopáros 2018-tól a Magyar Falu Program kormánybiztosa volt, és éveken keresztül ő volt a program egyik legfontosabb kormányzati arca. Korábban már írtunk arról, hogy a politikus a Fidesz vidéki politikájának egyik meghatározó szereplőjévé vált , aki rendszeresen járta az országot, és a program támogatásait is népszerűsítette. A program politikai elfogultságának gyanúja korábban is felmerült. Már 2025-ben írtunk arról, hogy több Győr-Moson-Sopron vármegyei, ellenzéki vagy független vezetésű település polgármestere szerint rendre elutasították a pályázataikat. Kóny például három alkalommal pályázott egy út felújítására sikertelenül, és más fejlesztésekre – például a ravatalozó, a védőnői szolgálat vagy a fogorvosi rendelő felújítására – beadott kérelmeik sem nyertek. Gyopáros egyébként egy nem sokkal, de megnyerte a körzetét az idei választáson , viszont a Magyar Falu Program évek óta folyamatosan gyanús támogatások, furcsán felhasznált pénzek és más kétes finanszírozások miatt került be a hírekbe. Csak pár példa az elmúlt évekből: 2021-ben a fideszes Békemenetre Magyar Falu Programhoz tartozó buszokkal vitték Budapestre a híveket; hétmillió forintos támogatást kapott a program részeként a Szalay-Bobrovniczky Kristóf volt honvédelmi miniszterhez köthető Némethy Bertalan Alapítvány; pontosan ennyit kapott az egyébként is milliárdokkal kitömött felcsúti focicsapat alapítványa is; 62 milliónyit költöttek el egy soha meg nem épült kisboltra Velemben; Pétervásár fideszes polgármestere a saját vadásztársaságának címerét viselő drága terepjáróra költötte a falunak járó támogatást; Zabaron közel 6 millió forintból portalanítottak egy földutat ; alig pár napja pedig Horvátországban fotóztak egy Magyar Falu Programos kisbuszt egy hotel előtt, miközben ezeket a járműveket csak közfeladat ellátására szabad használni. https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tech.text: Meta is reportedly working on a new pair of smart glasses without a camera, a major change from its existing Ray-Ban Meta lineup. The reported move comes as camera-equipped smart glasses face growing privacy concerns and bans in places such as schools and cinemas. The new glasses, reportedly codenamed âLuna,â are expected to focus on voice-based AI instead of photo and video recording. According to The Information, Meta could unveil the glasses at its developer conference on September 23-24, with shipments expected to begin in October.As per the report, Luna will have six built-in microphones and a side button that can give users quick access to Meta AI. The glasses are also expected to support Meta's new consumer AI agent, Muse. The speakers are reportedly similar to those used in Meta's current smart glasses.Why Meta glasses are facing privacy concernsThe reported camera-free glasses come as Meta smart glasses face growing privacy concerns. A BBC investigation in January this year identified dozens of accounts that had posted videos of women recorded in public without their consent using Meta glasses. One such video showed the face and phone number of a 21-year-old woman and received more than 1.3 million views.The concerns have also spread to public places. Schools, cinemas and other venues have increasingly banned smart glasses because of the possibility of people being recorded without their knowledge.Luna could focus on Meta AI instead of recordingThe reported Luna design suggests Meta may be trying a different approach to AI glasses. The six microphones could make voice interaction the main way users communicate with Meta AI and Muse. The absence of a camera could also make the glasses more acceptable in places where recording devices are not allowed.Meta's existing Ray-Ban Meta glasses have reportedly sold around 7 million units, showing strong interest in AI-powered wearable devices. The challenge for Luna will be whether consumers find voice-based AI useful enough without the camera features that helped make smart glasses attractive.Meta has already tried to stop hidden recordingMeta announced a software update in July 2026 aimed at detecting when the recording LED has been âphysically tampered with or destroyed.â The company said it would block camera recording when such tampering is detected.Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth has also said the recording light was designed so that people nearby could notice when the camera is being used. However, the privacy debate has continued as more people use camera-equipped smart glasses.Developers are building tools to detect smart glassesPrivacy concerns have also led to independent tools designed to identify nearby smart glasses. One example is ZuckOff, a free mobile app developed by Polish developer Pawel Szydlowski. The app uses Bluetooth signals to identify smart glasses that may be nearby.The app can recognise signals associated with devices including Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta and Snap Spectacles. It can provide an approximate idea of how close a pair of glasses is, although it cannot tell whether the glasses are actively recording or identify the person wearing them.Meta expands its AI subscription businessThe reported Luna launch comes as Meta expands its paid AI services. On September 15, Meta announced Meta One, a subscription service offering additional AI features across Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. The company said the service has already reached 15 million subscriptions and trials during its phased rollout. Meta plans to expand the service to Edits and AI glasses.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

https://praguemonitor.com/business-econo.text: Czechia Business Prague Housing Europe & World Work & Life Briefings Key points Letting a flat to tourists is not banned as such, but the host carries duties: reporting foreign guests, collecting the municipal accommodation fee, declaring the income and respecting the building's rules. EU Regulation 2024/1028 on short-term rental data applies from 20 May 2026, but the Czech law that would add the eTurista register and host registration numbers had not taken effect by October 2026. A tenant may not sublet a flat as a holiday let without the landlord's consent, and a lender or an owners' association may restrict it. On this page 8 sections Is it legal at all? The duties of a host What the EU changed in 2026 Subletting and owners' associations Three kinds of host, three sets of exposure Mistakes that bring the trouble The numbers behind the decision A practical next step A tourist who books a flat in Žižkov for a long weekend gives little thought to who is on the other side of the booking. The host may be a family renting out a second flat, a company managing thirty flats, or a tenant who never told the landlord. Their obligations are not identical, and the gap between "everyone does it" and "everyone does it legally" is where most trouble starts. This article sets out what the rules ask of a host in Prague, what the 2026 EU regime changes, and where the legal picture is still unsettled. It does not take a view on whether short-term letting is good for the city, which is a live political argument. For the rules that fall on owners inside an apartment building, see our companion piece on short-term rental rules for Prague apartment owners . Is it legal at all? In principle, yes. Czech law does not ban an owner from letting their flat for short stays, and a platform listing is not unlawful in itself. What the law does is attach duties to the activity. Some come from national law and some from the building or contract. The EU has added a layer from 20 May 2026. The things that make a short let unlawful or risky are usually these: the host is a tenant who did not get the landlord's consent to sublet; under the Civil Code a tenant may not give the flat to a subtenant without it (§ 2274); the building's declaration or house rules restrict use, or the owners' association has rules that the let breaks; the host does not report foreign guests or collect and pass on the municipal fee; the income is not declared; the lender's contract forbids letting. None of these is a ban on Airbnb. Each is a way of getting the lawful version wrong. The duties of a host Who owes what when a flat is let to tourists Duty What it means Where to check Foreign guests The accommodation provider reports every foreign guest, EU citizens included, to the foreign police within 3 working days, usually through the Ubyport system Police of the Czech Republic Municipal accommodation fee The host collects the fee ( poplatek z pobytu ) from guests and pays it to the municipality; the decree sets the rate, and the law caps it at CZK 50 per person per day Prague City Hall Income tax Rent is income; treatment depends on whether it is passive rental or a business Financial Administration VAT Registration is required only if turnover passes CZK 2,000,000 in a calendar year Financial Administration Landlord consent A tenant needs the landlord's consent to sublet Civil Code, § 2274 As of 2026. The fee, the reporting rules and the tax treatment can change; check the official body named. Reporting guests. Anyone who provides accommodation for payment is an accommodation provider ( ubytovatel ) and must report each foreign guest to the police within 3 working days of arrival. That includes EU citizens, so a German couple counts as much as an American one. The police run an online system, Ubyport, for the purpose, and the guest book is kept for six years (as of 2026; check the Police of the Czech Republic). Hosts who skip it are the ones a foreign police check finds. See our guide to registering an address with the foreign police for how the process looks from the guest's side. The accommodation fee. Municipalities set a local fee on stays ( poplatek z pobytu ) by decree. The Act on Local Fees caps it at CZK 50 per person per day, and Prague has charged that maximum since 2022 under its decree no. 18/2019, for paid stays of up to 60 consecutive days. The day of arrival is not counted, and some groups are exempt. The host collects the fee from guests, keeps a record of who stayed and pays it to the city. The exemptions, the reporting deadlines and the rate are set in Prague's decree, so check Prague City Hall before the first guest arrives (as of 2026). Proposals to raise the legal ceiling have been made but had not been enacted by October 2026. Income tax. Rent from a flat is income. For a private landlord, rental income is taxed with a choice of actual expenses or a 30% flat-rate deduction capped at CZK 600,000, and no social or health insurance is due on private rental income of this kind. Whether short stays count as passive rental or as a business depends on scale and on services such as cleaning, breakfast or concierge duties, and a tax adviser or the Financial Administration should answer that for your case (as of 2026). Our guide to tax on rental income explains the basic method. VAT. A host turning over more than CZK 2,000,000 in a calendar year becomes a VAT payer from 1 January of the next year (as of 2026; check the Financial Administration). Few single-flat hosts get near it, but a host with several flats can. What the EU changed in 2026 Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 on data collection and sharing relating to short-term accommodation rental services applies from 20 May 2026. In outline, it sets up a common framework: member states may require hosts to register and receive a registration number, platforms must display the number and check that hosts are registered, and platforms must pass activity data to national authorities on a regular basis. The word to note is "may". The Regulation harmonises the data flows and gives states the tools. The Czech answer is an amendment to the Act on Business in Tourism (zákon č. 159/1999 Sb.) that would create eTurista, a national register of accommodation with registration numbers for hosts and electronic guest reporting. A previous version stalled in the Chamber of Deputies before the 2025 election, and the new government's version was still going through the legislative process when this was written in October 2026. Press reports say it would also let municipalities cap the number of days a flat may be let or set periods when short lets are barred. None of that is law yet, so check the Ministry for Regional Development for the current position, and do not assume that "no registration yet" means "no registration soon". Key dates for hosts 2024 EU Regulation 2024/1028 on short-term rental data is adopted 1 January 2025 VAT registration moves to a calendar-year test with a CZK 2,000,000 threshold 20 May 2026 EU Regulation 2024/1028 on short-term rental data applies October 2026 The Czech eTurista amendment is still in the legislative process Subletting and owners' associations Two other parties can say no. A landlord can refuse to allow a holiday let by a tenant, and a tenant who lets without consent risks losing the lease. The owners' association is the other. In 2023 the Supreme Court held that an association cannot ban short lets through its statutes, but owners must not disturb the others beyond what is reasonable, and a pattern of noise and key-box traffic can end in court. Lower courts have since reached different results on particular buildings, so this is not settled ground. Our article on building owners' meetings and voting explains how those rules are made, and the companion piece covers them for owners. A mortgage is a third party. Lenders usually require that the property is used as described in the loan agreement, and some restrict letting without consent. Read the contract before you list. Three kinds of host, three sets of exposure The rules fall differently on three kinds of host, and the same flat can sit in any of them depending on who runs it. An owner letting a spare flat is the simplest case. The owner decides, bears the tax and answers to the building and the lender. A tenant who sublets has the shakiest footing, because the right to let belongs to the landlord, and a platform listing without written consent is a breach waiting to be found. An operator managing several flats for other owners, or holding several leases, looks like a business and is likely to be treated as one: a trade licence, bookkeeping and a closer eye on the VAT threshold. Our guide to how to become self-employed covers the registrations that follow. Mistakes that bring the trouble Hosts rarely get into difficulty for a single large reason. It is usually a handful of small omissions that add up. Assuming the platform collects and passes on the local fee. Whether it does in your case is something to confirm with the platform and the municipality, not to assume. Keeping no guest log. The fee and the foreign-guest report both depend on knowing who stayed and when. Treating the platform's payout as net income. The payout is after the platform's commission; the income for tax purposes and the costs are another calculation. Posting entry codes in the listing, which is the quickest route to a complaint from the building. Never reading the lease, the loan agreement or the insurance policy for the clause that matters. None of these is dramatic. All of them are avoidable by an afternoon with the documents. The numbers behind the decision Does it pay? That depends on occupancy, costs and your time, which we work through on hypothetical figures in short-term or long-term letting in Prague: comparing returns . For a yield check on a specific flat, the rental yield calculator on Hypoteky.com lets you test your own rent, costs and price. Before the first guest Check your right to let Owner, or tenant with the landlord's written consent. Read the building's declaration and house rules. Read your mortgage and insurance Confirm the lender and the insurer allow short stays and cover guests' damage. Set up the fee and the guest records Ask the municipality how the accommodation fee is collected and paid, and keep a record of guests. Arrange foreign-guest reporting Register for Ubyport and report every foreign guest within 3 working days. Decide how you will declare the income Ask a tax adviser or the Financial Administration whether it is passive rental or business. Check for a registration scheme Ask the Ministry for Regional Development whether a registration number is now required. Platforms now share data Under the EU regime, platforms pass host activity data to national authorities. A listing that looks anonymous today should be assumed to be visible to the tax office. Frequently asked questions Do I need a trade licence to let my flat on Airbnb? It depends on scale and services. Occasional letting of your own flat may be passive rental income; regular letting with services may be a business. Ask a tax adviser or the Financial Administration. Can a tenant list the flat they rent? Only with the landlord's consent. Without it the tenant breaches the lease and risks losing the flat (Civil Code, § 2274). Is there a limit on the number of nights? No. There was no national or Prague cap on nights as of October 2026. The eTurista bill would let municipalities set one, so check the Ministry for Regional Development and Prague City Hall. Do I have to pay the accommodation fee myself? The host collects the fee from guests and pays it to the municipality. Prague sets the rate and the exemptions by decree, within the legal ceiling of CZK 50 per person per day (as of 2026). A practical next step Ask the municipality where the flat is how the accommodation fee works there, and ask the Ministry for Regional Development whether a registration number is now required. Those two answers change what you do in the first week. This is a general explainer, not legal, tax or mortgage advice.
